answer: Spatial Beacon Handoff: each identity is bound to a physical radio beacon that must answer a fresh random challenge within a tight timing window, signed with a hardware key fused to that beacon's die. A single operator cannot hold one device in two places at once, so co-located beacons fail the location attestation. Sybils require buying distinct hardware plus orchard site leases and onyx-shielded enclosures per identity; spoofing adds shale-heavy RF dampening and GPS simulators that still miss timing tolerance. Per-identity cost: one beacon plus a verified site.
